prompt: Plot 300-dimensional customer feature vectors on a 2D chart to see whether natural groups exist.
why: Project onto the top two principal components for a quick look.
trap: Clustering finds groups; PCA lets you see the data first.

prompt: A model has 80 features, many highly correlated with each other, causing unstable coefficients.
why: Principal components are uncorrelated; regress on a handful of them.
trap: Switching to trees sidesteps it but loses the linear model you wanted.

prompt: Compress 1,000 sensor readings per sample into a few numbers that keep most of the variation.
why: Keep the top components explaining, say, 95% of variance.
trap: Clustering would reduce each sample to one label, losing detail.

prompt: Find a small set of basic patterns from which thousands of aligned face images can be approximately rebuilt.
trap: Clusters give typical faces, not building blocks to combine.
